title: fix(backup): inspect scratch payloads after lifetime admission
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backup scratch repair can report a false preservation warning when an active SQLite snapshot commits between directory enumeration and file inspection, removing its rollback journal.

## User Impact

Doctor classifies live scratch as active before inspecting a payload that its current owner is still changing. Abandoned scratch keeps the existing guarded reclamation path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move token-backed repair inspection behind the existing exclusive lifetime admission. Dry-run and tokenless legacy inspection retain their behavior. Root identity, ownership, symlink, retirement and release checks remain authoritative; no new lock, schema, retry or timeout is introduced.

Production: +5/-1 (net +4), required to respect the existing lifetime boundary. Regression tests: +39/-0.

## Evidence

Current head `94085dc8a54b9e66cf90982f9d9bc5e0ebd6175f` replays only this two-file fix onto frozen main `83d133328796976239ce5f4806dd52bfafdf686a`. Both final patch blobs and both baseline owner/test blobs match the preceding reviewed head `7827dfacd72e3772c31ff809979c73a4fd77d6e3` and its base. The base includes the independent [Matrix fixture lifetime repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155679), [SSH fixture teardown repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155643), [accepted-approval fixture repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155574), and [Doctor retained-agent admission fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e99e75e2e60a48875d63f6d84a3db4882ca00252). No other repair is replayed in this PR.

Fresh exact-head P0–P2 review found no actionable finding. That review is scoped: the lifetime-token dependency attachment was omitted, and no runtime was run on the new head. Separate maintainer source review verified the token, private-directory, SQLite-error and rooted filesystem owners unchanged from the previously reviewed repair. Current-head hosted CI qualified in [run 35722510540, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35722510540/attempts/2). The [generated exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35722544982) found no actionable finding, security concern, risk or rank-up move and withdrew the migration-proof premise. Its durable review comment still references the preceding head while current publication is queued; the generated report is not represented as a published current-head comment.

- A real SQLite commit between `readdir` and `lstat` reproduces the old `ENOENT`; the regression classifies active scratch without touching its journal.
- Current hosted proof tested merge `1bae5cc943ceacf6b5d0e4fea1823ffe36894fe0` (base `927c57a706acb7a7621be101637c1e40f6c2941c` plus head `94085dc8`). [All 13 scratch cases and the actual 27-file/369-case owner group passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35722510540/job/106728850563), including the real-journal regression. The [storage sibling group passed 1,406 cases with 2 skips](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35722510540/job/106728850756), including all 8 retained-agent cases; 58 files passed and 1 was skipped.
- Attempt 1 had one unrelated producer failure: the Gateway clock-jump test retained an agent turn in its pending queue after 31.251 seconds. The backup change does not modify that fixture or its reviewed queue owners. [One job-specific qualification continuation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35722510540/job/106734798381) passed all 325 cases with the same tested merge and ordered two-config/23-file input. Its environment changed from Node 24.19, 2 CPUs, 8.22 GB and global worker budget 2 to Node 24.21, 4 CPUs, 16.77 GB and budget 3. The original failure remains causally unresolved; this is qualification, not evidence of a causal fix or an equivalent environment. Only that producer and the dependent aggregate ran again. The final 137-job projection is 120 successes and 17 skips, including 135 preserved earlier rows.
- Historical matching-byte Linux Node 24.19 qualification passed 20 complete scratch-file executions (13 cases each) and three original 26-file/367-case selections. Measured scratch wrapper wall time was 1.440–2.130 seconds. No literal `--maxWorkers=1` claim is made.
- At preceding head `7827dfac`, the 13 scratch cases and 26-file/367-case owner group passed. The retained-agent cases and storage group also passed (8 retained-agent cases; 1,462 storage passes and 2 skips). The old run's Matrix and SSH failures stay historical; their independent repairs now exist on the frozen base.
- Exact fs-safe 0.18.0 rooted mutation and identity contracts were inspected.

The earlier `afe03bfd` [Doctor failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35709212998/job/106685843975) reached a strict alias guard before retained-agent exclusion; the separate landed Doctor fix repaired that order. A pristine-state Doctor child timeout remains unexplained. No retry, timeout increase or speculative product change is included.

This journal race was discovered during investigation. It is not attributed to an original CI job or the separate opaque-link warning-count failure. Historical matching-byte tests are not relabeled as execution on the rebased current head.

## Review follow-through

The preceding-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155546#issuecomment-5772591410) retracted the migration premise. Maintainer disposition remains explicit: migration/upgrade conversion is inapplicable to this ordering-only change. Schema/version, serialized token and journal formats, defaults, configuration, principals and permissions are unchanged. Existing active, abandoned, legacy, unexpected-content, symlink and partial-cleanup regressions cover the preserved contracts. No migration, backfill or new migration test is warranted; generated compatibility checkboxes do not change that source-backed disposition.

Named follow-up: correct ClawSweeper's path-based migration/backfill classification for ordering-only repairs with unchanged stored-data contracts. No ClawSweeper implementation change is part of this PR.
